blocks.text: Hello! My name is Amelia Herlina, an international student from Indonesia. I graduated from Tarumanagara University with a degree in Architecture. I am interested in sustainable design, urban architecture and historical architecture.

blocks.label: Research Focus
bullets: Studied the relationship between human activity, nature, and the environment.
Used the COVID-19 period as a case to observe changes in human behavior and environmental conditions.
Examined how human actions affect the environment and how environmental quality affects people's daily life and well-being.
Developed a design that focuses on human-centered and environmentally responsive architecture.

blocks.label: Research Method
bullets: Concept development based on the idea of an oasis as a place of shelter and refuge.
Spatial experiments using light, shadow, and water to study atmosphere and perception.
Design exploration inspired by Lebbeus Woods' speculative approach to architecture.

blocks.label: Research Outcome
bullets: Designed an experimental learning and working space as an architectural proposal.
Developed mass composition inspired by water ripple patterns.

images.alt: A water passage framed by monumental concrete walls and columns
Public space and water beneath the elevated structure
images.heading: Urban condition
images.body: Zhongshan is experienced as a set of disconnected conditions: a static park, streets made mainly for movement, and an intense night market. The project begins with the missing condition between them—a place where people can walk, pause, stay, and interact.
images.caption: Urban condition / An in-between space

images.alt: Human-scale view along the canal edge
images.heading: Hidden canal
images.body: Beneath the site lies a canal connected to Taipei’s historic Liugongjun irrigation system. Once a visible network linking agriculture and urban life, much of it disappeared below roads as Taipei urbanized. The proposal brings this water infrastructure back into the public imagination.
images.caption: Site and context / The concealed waterway

images.alt: Atmospheric view of the water passage
images.caption: Interlude / Water, light, and concrete

images.alt: Architectural view responding to the underpass condition
images.heading: Existing condition
images.body: The underpass is currently defined by low activity, an uncomfortable pedestrian edge, poor environmental quality, and little opportunity for social use. Its infrastructure separates the neighborhood even though water, schools, housing, and public movement already meet here.
images.caption: Existing condition / Underused infrastructure

images.alt: Concrete passage reconnecting people with water
images.heading: Reveal · Connect · Activate
images.body: The design follows three actions. Reveal the buried canal and use water for passive cooling. Connect street level to the canal with a new public layer. Activate the passage with landscape and programs for rest, study, everyday exchange, and seasonal events.
images.caption: Design strategy / Reveal, connect, activate

images.alt: Public passage designed for changing daily activities
images.heading: A changing daily rhythm
images.body: The passage changes through the day. Morning routes support walking and breakfast stalls; afternoon shade creates places to rest and interact; evening circulation can expand into a night market and other collective activities. Architecture becomes a framework for time as well as movement.
images.caption: Program / Morning to evening

images.alt: Full view of public life around the reopened waterway
images.caption: Interlude / The urban commons

images.alt: Monumental concrete structure reflected in water
images.heading: Brutalism as an approach
images.body: Exposed concrete expresses material honesty and makes the structure legible. Stepped, tectonic forms bring people into direct contact with water, while durable, low-maintenance materials support long-term public use. Monumental elements are balanced by intimate paths, shade, and reflections.
images.caption: Material approach / Exposed concrete

projects.title: Cynefin

images.alt: Aerial view of Cynefin's looping form and landscaped ground
Reflective looping building surrounded by trees and mist
images.heading: A place of belonging
images.body: Cynefin imagines a place where people and animals belong within a shared natural world. Developed as a university studio proposal for life after the pandemic, it brings informal workspaces, a public park and a speculative holographic zoo together. Digital encounters with wildlife invite learning without keeping animals in captivity.
images.caption: University studio / Post-pandemic dwelling space

images.alt: Concept illustration of working beside an imagined oasis
images.heading: The oasis
images.body: The oasis becomes a metaphor for relief from confinement and the pressures of working online. Water, planting and shade form a setting for rest and concentration. The proposal treats contact with nature as part of everyday work and learning, creating a calmer environment within the city.
images.caption: Concept / Nature as a daily refuge

images.alt: Oblique aerial view showing the continuous loop and central landscape
images.caption: Interlude / A landscape held within a loop

images.alt: Line drawing of the undulating building volume and ground-level canopy
images.heading: Water, light and shadow
images.body: The form studies draw on falling droplets, expanding ripples and the rebound of water. These movements inform a continuous, undulating building loop. Reflections and changing light extend the experiment into the experience of the building, while the lower landscape connects the elevated volume to its surroundings.
images.caption: Form study / Droplets, ripples and rebound

images.alt: Exploded circulation diagram with coloured routes between levels
images.heading: A layered journey
images.body: An ocean journey at ground level connects to rainforest and Africa trails above. Informal workspaces, a café and an outdoor plaza bring everyday activity into the same setting. The circulation diagram distinguishes pedestrian routes, visitor trails and vehicle access, showing how these experiences unfold across several levels.
images.caption: Program / Work, leisure and wildlife learning

images.alt: Water courtyard with speculative holographic wildlife and reflective architecture
images.caption: Interlude / An imagined encounter with wildlife

images.alt: Exploded architectural model showing the layered loop within its urban context
images.caption: Spatial organization / Ground, trails and elevated loop

images.alt: North-south section through the trails, workspace and outdoor plaza

images.alt: Two cutaway details of the layered envelope and display assembly
images.heading: An experimental envelope
images.body: The detail studies explore a layered envelope combining GRP panels, galvanized steel, insulation and glazing. Display components support the proposal's imagined digital environments. These drawings describe a speculative assembly for the studio concept rather than a completed construction system.
images.caption: Detail study / Structure, skin and display layers
